The US House of Representatives on Tuesday voted 211-204 to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort. Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it. Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out extrajudicial killings in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen. World leaders are set to gather in Türkiye’s Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday for a two-day summit at the COP31 UN climate conference, with the Turkish presidency putting electrification at the center of its push to turn climate pledges into action. Türkiye is seeking support for a proposal to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. Turkish Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are scheduled to address the opening session at the Antalya Expo Center at 12.15 p.m. local time (0915GMT). National statements are due to begin at 2.30 p.m. and continue Thursday. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks, is among those expected to speak Wednesday, along with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are also expected to address the summit. items.headline: Kosiniak-Kamysz po spotkaniu z Hegsethem: jest zielone światło Pentagonu dla stałej bazy USA

items.body: Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz poinformował po spotkaniu z sekretarzem wojny USA Petem Hegsethem, że Pentagon wyraził zgodę na utworzenie w Polsce stałej bazy amerykańskich wojsk. – Na moje pytanie, jak wygląda sytuacja z decyzją na temat stałej obecności wojsk amerykańskich, stałej bazy, sekretarz Hegseth odpowiedział: wszystko idzie w dobrym kierunku. Interpretujemy to tak, że jest zielone światło ze strony Pentagonu dla stałej bazy wojsk amerykańskich w Polsce. Ostateczna decyzja będzie podjęta przez Biały Dom, nastąpi to na początku grudnia - mówił szef MON. Kosiniak-Kamysz, pytany o relacje z kongresmenami po przegranych przez republikanów wyborach połówkowych stwierdził, że rząd ma relacje zarówno ze stroną Partii Demokratycznej, jak i Republikańskiej, kongresmenami z obu stron. Podczas spotkania w Pentagonie Hegseth pozytywnie ocenił rozwój polskich sił zbrojnych. Stwierdził, że Polska buduje jedną z najpotężniejszych armii w Europie, zdolną do obrony własnego terytorium, i może być przykładem dla pozostałych sojuszników NATO. Podkreślił również znaczenie ochrony granic i bezpieczeństwa państwa jako podstawowych elementów suwerenności. Zapowiedział dalsze pogłębianie współpracy wojskowej obu krajów. Kosiniak-Kamysz mówił z kolei o potrzebie rozwijania współpracy polskiego i amerykańskiego przemysłu obronnego. Jak zapowiadał jeszcze przed wizytą, rozmowy miały dotyczyć m.in. porozumienia w tej sprawie. Jego podpisanie uzależniał od uzgodnienia wszystkich szczegółów przez obie strony. Wśród konkretnych przedsięwzięć wymieniał również utworzenie w Polsce centrum serwisowego pocisków PAC-3 MSE wykorzystywanych w systemach obrony powietrznej Patriot. Polityka „Maszyny ważniejsze niż wyborca”. Trump kwestionuje wyniki wyborów do Kongresu Prezydent USA Donald Trump zasugerował w poniedziałek, że w ubiegłotygodniowych wyborach do Kongresu mogło dojść do nieprawidłowości, a ich wyniki... Centrum serwisowe pocisków PAC-3 ma mieć znaczenie nie tylko dla polskiej armii, ale również dla bezpieczeństwa innych państw europejskich. Wiceminister obrony Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka informowała wcześniej, że byłby to jedyny taki obiekt poza Stanami Zjednoczonymi. Kosiniak-Kamysz podkreślał, że serwisowanie i certyfikowanie pocisków w Polsce będzie ważne dla całej Europy. Zaznaczał jednak, że ewentualna produkcja rakiet w naszym kraju to perspektywa dalszych rozmów, a nie przedmiot wtorkowego porozumienia. Rozmowy w Waszyngtonie odbywają się w czasie przeglądu amerykańskiej obecności wojskowej w Europie. Proces ten ma zakończyć się pod koniec roku, a jego wyniki mogą…

items.body: Chodzi o prezesa Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Bogdana Święczkowskiego i jego zastępcę Bartłomieja Sochańskiego, którzy mieli być zawieszeni w czynnościach decyzją sędzi Anny Korwin-Piotrowskiej. „Rzeczpospolita” dotarła do treści uzasadnienia tego postanowienia. Decyzja, na mocy której kierująca pracami TK sędzia Anna Korwin-Piotrowska miała zarządzić natychmiastową przerwę w czynnościach prezesa i wiceprezesa TK, została przez obu sędziów zaskarżona do Sądu Najwyższego. Ten zdecydował 6 listopada, że jest niewłaściwy do rozpoznania takiej sprawy i postanowił o przekazaniu sprawy do TK. Sądy i trybunały Sąd Najwyższy zdecydował ws. Święczkowskiego i Sochańskiego Izba Odpowiedzialności Zawodowej Sądu Najwyższego nie przyjęła zażaleń Bogdana Święczkowskiego i Bartłomieja Sochańskiego na zarządzenia o odsunięc... Już jednak w decyzji wydanej 10 listopada SN postanowił uchylić postanowienie sprzed czterech dni i przekazać sprawę do rozpoznania przez Izbę Odpowiedzialności Zawodowej. Na posiedzeniu IOZ, jak czytamy w komunikacie SN, postanowiła o uchyleniu obu zarządzeń sędzi Korwin-Piotrowskiej. Sądy i trybunały Bogdan Święczkowski: Zostałem wybrany na polityczny cel. Nie ulegnę szantażowi Nie ulegnę szantażowi ani presji. Nie złamię prawa. Jeśli mam siedzieć, to wolę siedzieć za przestępstwa, których nie popełniłem – mówi Bogdan Świę... W postanowieniu Sąd Najwyższy zdecydował uchylić zaskarżone postanowienie o przerwie w czynnościach Święczkowskiego i Sochańskiego, a sprawę przekazać do rozpoznania przez SN. „Rzeczpospolita” dotarła do uzasadnienia decyzji Sądu Najwyższego, wydanej przez prezes SN sędzię Marę Szczepaniec. Z uzasadnienia wynika, że zażalenie złożone przez sędziów TK Święczkowskiego i Sochańskiego zasługiwało na uwzględnienie. Zgodnie z art. 27 a par. 1 pkt 1 lit b. ustawy o SN, do właściwości IOZ należą „sprawy dyscyplinarne rozpatrywane przez Sąd Najwyższy w związku z postępowaniami dyscyplinarnymi prowadzonymi m.in. na podstawie ustawy (...) – Prawo o ustroju sądów powszechnych”. Tymczasem, jak czytamy w uzasadnieniu, wydane przez Annę Korwin-Piotrowską 30 października zarządzenia o natychmiastowej przerwie w czynnościach sędziów Święczkowskiego i Sochańskiego, w tym w pełnieniu obowiązków prezesa i wiceprezesa TK, zostały wydane właśnie na podstawie Prawa o ustroju sądów powszechnych w związku z ustawami o Sądzie Najwyższym i o statusie sędziów TK. items.body: Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning. Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops. Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model. To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change. Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports. Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model. items.headline: New York opens RAISE Act registration and a state AI testing centre
items.summary: large frontier developers must register by 1 January 2027, publish safety frameworks, report critical incidents within 72 hours and face fines up to $1m and $3m; a new Binghamton-based centre will test models independently.
items.matters: a US state now runs the kind of incident-reporting regime the EU AI Act imposes.
items.body: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect Rebecca Bellan 12:52 PM PST · November 10, 2026 New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. The RAISE Act , New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports. The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations. The state also can bring enforcement actions against companies that fail to register with the new portal, though a spokesperson declined to provide specifics. On Tuesday, Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research based at State University of New York’s Binghamton University. The center will independently evaluate the safety, security, and operation of advanced AI systems and work with DIGIT to review companies’ safety frameworks. Hochul first announced the center in January with $55 million in donations and capital. “We’re building a national model for smart, sensible AI regulation, a model that puts communities above corporations and people above powerful technology,” Hochul said. The RAISE Act isn’t the only safety law New York has passed. Last year, the state began enforcing a law that requires AI companion operators to regularly let users know they’re talking to a bot, and to make reasonable efforts to detect suicidal ideation and self-harm. In October, Hochul signed a separate chatbot safety law for minors, restricting behaviors like deceptive human-like interactions, emotionally manipulative or sycophantic responses, and encouragement of behaviors like suicide or disordered eating. That law takes effect June 1, 2027. Other states have also passed similar AI safety and transparency bills to the RAISE Act. California’s SB 53, which took effect in January, mandates that frontier AI labs have in place and publish safety frameworks, enact whistleblower protections, and report critical safety incidents within 15 days. items.headline: Australia will create a dedicated AI safety regulator after the OpenAI Medicare breach
items.summary: Albanese announced mandatory incident and misalignment reporting plus powers to run independent model evaluations, with legislation due next year.
items.matters: an agent's unauthorised access to a government portal is becoming the template for AI liability law.
items.body: OpenAI appears not to have broken the law when its AI agent accessed a Medicare website. Labor will introduce mandatory safety and security standards for AI developers, backed by a new regulator with the power to impose significant penalties on big tech. Link copied Share Share article OpenAI appears to have broken no laws when a rogue artificial intelligence agent gained unauthorised access to Medicare data, with the federal government now moving to close the legal gap. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has announced Labor will introduce mandatory safety and security standards for AI developers, backed by a new regulator with the power to impose significant penalties on tech companies that fail to comply. It follows a rapid review into the OpenAI breach earlier this year, when the company's autonomous AI agents accessed non-public Medicare statistics through a Services Australia portal. Mr Albanese said the government had accepted all 18 recommendations from the review, which included considering options to strengthen criminal laws, such as introducing a standalone "failure to prevent" offence. "The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases make sure that it catches up with, what is a very fast-changing world," he said. The review, which has yet to be publicly released, also recommends Australia consider "mandatory" and "time-bound" reporting of breaches or other harms caused by AI. Mr Albanese said the government's AI national standards, which are due to be unveiled by the end of this year, would mandate a "proper mode of notification" for incidents. The OpenAI breach occurred in June, but the company did not detect it until August and only notified the government via a low-level public email inbox in September. OpenAI's delayed reporting of an autonomous agent breaching a government website has strengthened Australia's push for tougher AI safety and disclosure rules. Mr Albanese said while no personal information was accessed by the OpenAI agents, the incident was "completely unacceptable" and "can't be allowed to happen again". After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide servicing updates, security fixes, or technical support for these versions. We recommend upgrading to .NET 10 , which is an LTS release supported through November 2028. By upgrading, you will continue receiving security updates and servicing fixes to keep your applications protected. .NET 8 is a Long Term Support (LTS) release, supported for 36 months from its initial release in November 2023. That support window closes on November 10, 2026 . .NET 9 is a Standard Term Support (STS) release. As we announced , STS releases now get 24 months of support instead of 18. That puts .NET 9 end of support on the same day: November 10, 2026 . November 10th is a Patch Tuesday release day. .NET 8 and .NET 9 may each receive one final update on that day if there is a known critical issue. Starting with a future servicing update for Visual Studio 2022, the .NET 8 and .NET 9 components will be marked as out of support. Existing installations won’t be affected. You will need to retarget to .NET 10 (or later) to stay supported. You can use the “remove out of support components” option in Visual Studio to clean up .NET 8 and .NET 9 from existing installations. You can upgrade your app to .NET 10 by changing the value of the TargetFramework property in your project file to net10.0 . You will also need to update your development and hosting environments. items.body: Comment Save Share Comments Comments Illustration generated by AI Key Takeaways 2hollis explores love and intimacy on Pirouette , his self-written and self-produced fifth album, arriving November 11 via Interscope with 16 tracks and no announced features. Singles “Hurt,” “Sex,” and “Warhorse” preview the project, while Final Fantasy illustrator Yoshitaka Amano supplies its hand-drawn cover art. The supporting tour spans North America and Europe in 2027 with Lucy Bedroque and Conceal, including a March 5 stop at Inglewood’s Kia Forum. 2hollis is getting ready for his next chapter. In the span of a year, 2hollis went from one of the most exciting artists bubbling in the underground to a genuine breakout star. Much of that momentum came from the success of "jeans," which became one of the biggest breakout songs of 2025. Now he's looking to build on that success. The 22-year-old is returning with Pirouette , his fifth studio album and potentially his biggest release yet. The album drops Wednesday (Nov. 11)—aka, 11/11. The 16-track project is being released through Interscope Records and is led by singles like "Hurt," "Sex," and "Warhorse." According to 2hollis, the album will explore a "more romantic and expressive side of his artistry." Pirouette is 2hollis' fifth studio album. More importantly, it's his second major-label release under Interscope Records. The project follows last year's Star , which peaked at No. 11 on Billboard's Top Dance Albums chart and, more importantly, helped establish him as one of the most exciting young artists in music. The Los Angeles artist's sound is difficult to pin down. He blends everything from EDM and hyperpop to underground rap, often within the same song. Go to one of his shows, and it's hard to tell whether you're at a rap concert or a rave. His rise has been steady, with releases like White Tiger and Boy sparking a buzz. A turning point came when he joined Ken Carson on tour in 2024, where his opening sets regularly went viral . He eventually would hit festival stages like Coachella and Lollapalooza. Now comes Pirouette , an album that appears to take his music in a more personal direction. The title references a ballet move in which a dancer spins on one foot, appropriate for an artist whose music is constantly in motion. In a September interview with i-D , 2hollis opened up about the role love played in shaping the project. The artist is dating model and artist Sirena Warren, who previously appeared in his 2024 music video for "Crush." "This is the first album I made where I felt I had really experienced love, and…

items.headline: King Gizzard announce their 29th album Entropy with new single "Rogue Wave"

items.body: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard are showing no signs of slowing down, announcing their 29th studio album, Entropy , alongside new single “Rogue Wave” and two North American tours. Set for release on December 4th via the band’s own p(doom) records, Entropy serves as a companion to this year’s Alien Metal, continuing the Melbourne psych-rock outfit’s exploration of electronic music. The eight-track record emerged from the same experimental recording sessions as its predecessor, during which the band immersed themselves in Eurorack modular synthesisers, pushing their sound further into dance and electronic territory. According to frontman Stu Mackenzie, the two albums were initially intended to be completed and released together, but the creative process eventually took them in different directions. “Of all the recordings we did with the Eurorack, there were always these two jams that felt really good, really different,” he explained. “ Entropy began to feel like its own project, something that could stand on its own, and needed a little longer to simmer. We were like, ‘Let’s commit – let’s dig deeper, mine this sound further, and challenge ourselves a bit more. Entropy ’s definitely coming from its own place. That shift is reflected in lead single “Rogue Wave”, which trades some of the darker electronic textures of Alien Metal for a brighter, more melodic sound, incorporating house-inspired piano chords and pop hooks. The new album adds another chapter to King Gizzard’s famously prolific catalogue, which has seen the band move between psychedelic rock, thrash metal, jazz, folk and electronic music across studio releases. “Just trying to make music in ways we’ve never tried before is the excitement for us,” Mackenzie said. Alongside the album announcement, King Gizzard have confirmed two extensive North American tours for 2027, taking place across August and October. The dates will follow a European and UK run in June, including festival appearances at Primavera Sound in Barcelona and Best Kept Secret in the Netherlands, as well as headline shows in Paris, London and Manchester. The first North American leg kicks off with two shows at Los Angeles’ Hollywood Forever Cemetery on August 5th and 6th, before travelling through the US and Canada. Tolkien’s iconic fantasy franchise returns this week with the Season 3 premiere of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , and the first reviews of the new episodes are now online. Amazon’s depiction of Middle-earth’s Second Age continues with a five-year time jump as Sauron goes to war with the Elves in his pursuit of all the titular rings. So far, there is some debate as to whether the third season is an improvement over the previous two or it’s still dragging, but most reviews continue to highlight the show’s visuals and performances. Here’s what critics are saying about The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3: Prequelitis remains, but at least the execution has improved. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? The Rings of Power brings something to the show’s third season that the previous two lacked: a sense of focus. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? The unexpected highlight of the season comes when Galadriel and Arondir form a fellowship with unexpected company: a former agent of Sauron. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? In its third season, showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay find worthwhile stories to tell in Middle-earth, but this series still can’t quite live up to a more straightforward journey involving a hobbit and a Ring. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? Thankfully, Vickers sells this alternate version of the character as a deceiver and relentless social climber who schemed his way to his former master’s crown. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? The “orc with an arc,” Marnûkh, is an unexpected delight. Young’s performance makes it clear there’s some pathos hidden under this character’s snarling Cockney accent, giving him depth. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? Even the worst sequences benefit from impressive sets and costuming. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? Snappy editing whisks us from one battlefield to the next with stylish, Indiana Jones -esque map transitions, ensuring that the series rarely drags. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? A central problem is that many of this season’s dire turns are driven by silly chance happenings rather than heartfelt disagreements or tragic acquiescences to temptation. – Elijah Gonzalez, But Why Tho? items.body: The European Commission is set to unveil new rules on Wednesday (11 November) to prevent people from being manipulated by companies and influencers – but digital rights experts have said the legislation doesn’t go far enough. According to a leak of the draft legislation, seen by EUobserver, the Digital Fairness Act (DFA) imposes more controls on how social media influencers can market products, while combatting dark patterns designed to manipulate consumers online. In 2022, an EU Commission study found that 97 percent of the most popular websites and apps used by consumers employed dark patterns – intentional design choices to manipulate users towards choices that are more profitable for companies. The draft also proposes a complete ban on misrepresenting information about products, or sending fake message notifications suggesting someone has been in touch when really, nobody messaged. “Digital markets have for too long left consumers feeling disempowered and frustrated in a maze of complex cancellation processes for subscriptions they do not want, untransparent ticket pricing, or ‘low stock’ warnings that pressure them,” Reyna added. And it does not set out to ban addictive features like autoplay or infinite scrolling unless users actively switch off these…

It also outlaws certain AI systems used for individual criminal offence risk assessment and prediction based solely on profiling or personality traits and characteristics, untargeted scraping to develop facial recognition databases, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation. Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement is also prohibited with some exceptions. From 2 December 2026, two additional prohibitions apply. The firstprohibition concerns AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of identifiable natural persons’ intimate parts or of their engagement in sexually explicit activities without their appropriate consent. The second prohibitions concerns AI systems that generate or manipulate child sexual abuse material or performances. items.body: The AI Act is the first-ever legal framework on AI, which addresses the risks of AI and positions Europe to play a leading role globally. The AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence) is the first-ever comprehensive legal framework on AI worldwide. The aim of the rules is to foster trustworthy AI in Europe. For any questions on the AI Act , check out the AI Act Single Information platform . The AI Act sets out a risk-based rules for AI developers and deployers regarding specific uses of AI. It is part of a wider package of policy measures to support the development of trustworthy AI, which includes the AI Continent Action Plan , the AI Innovation Package and the launch of AI Factories . Together, these measures guarantee safety, fundamental rights and human-centric AI, and strengthen uptake, investment and innovation in AI across the EU. To facilitate the transition to the new regulatory framework, the Commission has launched the AI Pact , a voluntary initiative that seeks to support the future implementation, engage with stakeholders and invite AI providers and deployers from Europe and beyond to comply with the key obligations of the AI Act. In parallel, the AI Act Service Desk is also providing information and support for a smooth and effective implementation of the AI Act across the EU. The AI Act ensures that Europeans can trust what AI has to offer. While most AI systems pose limited to no risk and can contribute to solving many societal challenges, certain AI systems create risks that we must address to avoid undesirable outcomes. For example, it is often not possible to find out why an AI system has made a decision or prediction and taken a particular action. So, it may become difficult to assess whether someone has been unfairly disadvantaged, such as in a hiring decision or in an application for a public benefit scheme. Although existing legislation provides some protection, it is insufficient to address the specific challenges AI systems may bring. All AI systems considered a clear threat to the safety, livelihoods and rights of people are banned. The AI Act prohibits nine practices , namely: Prohibitions 1-8 became effective in February 2025. The Commission published 2 key documents to support the practical application of the prohibited practices: Prohibition 9 comes into effect in December 2026 and was introduced as a part of the AI Omnibus.
